phosphor.note: Live readout tint, DSEG gauge only.

readout.purpose: Exactly one element in the app: the Home TODAY kcal master readout. Live tint phosphor #f2ede2, idle ink-faint '----'.

voice-display.purpose: The stamp voice — earned-win banners only (ADDED TO PANTRY at 2.6rem). Shouting reserved for genuine wins.

voice-title.purpose: Screen titles (Pantry, Eat, Health) at variable weight 550.

voice-item.purpose: Entity names: products, insight titles, state headings.

voice-body.purpose: Primary prose at 15px/1.6 — insight bodies, empty-state instructions. Never carries numbers.

voice-micro.purpose: Unit captions and fine print under data values.

data-xl.purpose: Screen hero value — one per screen: the reading the screen exists to give (week average, item quantity, idle '----'). Always tabular-nums.

data-lg.purpose: Tile and counter values (macros, weekly counters).

data-md.purpose: Row values, the KCAL unit, the log voice on Eat.

data-sm.purpose: Metadata: provenance, timestamps, footers. Hairline 0.02em tracking.

data-micro.purpose: Axis endpoints, engraved unit suffixes, sparkline day labels.

keycap.purpose: The one engraving standard on every pressable control: mono, uppercase, 0.12em.

keycap-sm.purpose: Compact key engraving (nav keys, SCAN caption); drops tracking to 0.06em under 350px viewports rather than wrapping.

label.purpose: Uppercase mono micro-label (0.14em, ink-faint) that self-labels every module, nav key, and the top-bar nameplate — panel printing, never decoration.

shadows.name: key-ledge
shadows.purpose: The single shadow in the system: the machined lower edge of the orange action key. Collapses to 0 with translateY(2px) on :active. Structural pressed-key device; never used off keys.

motion.name: motion-state
motion.purpose: Small state changes, toasts, splits, slot-ins.

motion.name: motion-nav
motion.purpose: Plate travel between screens — native cadence (push/cover/uncover).

motion.name: motion-wipe
motion.purpose: Analysis wipes — the duration is the message.

motion.name: plate-travel
motion.value: two-plate choreography: outgoing <main> cloned into a fixed .plate-ghost clip layer across the body swap; push = incoming full-width slide + outgoing 32% parallax with dim; cover = tool rises over receding desk (scale .97); uncover = tool slides off downward over the brightening desk; 320ms ease-travel
motion.purpose: Navigation choreography — old and new plates travel together like a native OS stack, chassis bolted still. Reduced motion: no ghost, 120ms opacity-only.

motion.name: wipe-busy / wipe-in
motion.value: phosphor scanline loop 1.3s / clip-path inset reveal 420ms
motion.purpose: Background analysis in flight / freshly settled result. Gone under reduced motion.

motion.name: split
motion.purpose: A surface parts to reveal controls (disclosures, inline forms).

motion.name: slot-in
motion.purpose: A new plate seats into a stack.

motion.name: led-sweep
motion.purpose: Success sweep on reward stamps; the wipe in LED form.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.purpose: Reward stamps and toasts land like a press.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: Physical key acknowledgment; disabled while a request is in flight.

breakpoints.name: shell-max
breakpoints.purpose: max-w-md single-column console shell; seam-edged (md:border-x) on wider viewports.

breakpoints.name: narrow-chassis
breakpoints.purpose: At or below this width, keycap-sm engraving trades tracking (0.12em -> 0.06em) for fit rather than wrapping.

narrative.overview:
Jabba's app surface is a piece of dark tabletop hardware, not a wellness feed. Every screen is a matte near-black chassis carrying seam-separated module plates; every module silkscreens its own uppercase mono micro-label in the top-left, the way a synthesizer labels a knob. Numbers are instrument readings — tabular mono everywhere, and one seven-segment master readout for the day's kilocalories. Color is functional signal, never mood: five fixed-meaning lamps on an otherwise achromatic machine.

The console is the user's, not the brand's: the status bar carries the user's name, and the machine reports only what it actually measured. When the machine doesn't know, it says so — '----', 'NO DATA', an unlit LED, an empty meter track — never a fabricated zero. When the user genuinely completes the loop, the reward fires as hardware: a full green field, an LED sweep, a stamped check, counters that tick. Nothing celebratory happens without a real trigger.

This is one committed dark world. There is no light mode and no appearance toggle; html.dark is hard-set and the browser chrome (selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring) is tuned to the console.
keyCharacteristics: Matte near-black chassis; plates separated by 1px hairline seams; no ambient shadows.
Every module self-labels with a silkscreen mono micro-label.
If it's measured, it's mono; if it's spoken, it's grotesk.
Five fixed-meaning signal colors on small areas; the machine is otherwise achromatic.
Honest unknowns: '----' / 'NO DATA' / empty tracks, never invented zeros.
Rewards are hardware events (green field, LED sweep, stamp, ticking counters), earned only.

rules.name: The Fixed-Meaning Rule
rules.body: The five signals carry fixed semantics (action, good, low, high, info) on small areas only. A signal color is never decorative, never a background wash, and never re-assigned. The single exception is the earned success stamp's full green field.

rules.name: The Black-on-Signal Rule
rules.body: Text and glyphs sitting on any signal fill are pure black (#000). Signals are lamps; lamps don't carry grey type.

rules.name: The One-Fill Band Grammar
rules.body: Qualitative band chips share one grammar: solid signal fill + black text (GOOD/OK → green, OK at 70% opacity; LOW → amber; HIGH → red). Unknown bands get no fill — seam-strong border, ink-faint text, label 'NO DATA'.

rules.name: The Measured/Spoken Rule
rules.body: If it's measured, it's mono; if it's spoken, it's grotesk. No number ever renders in Archivo; no sentence ever renders in Fragment Mono.

rules.name: The One Readout Rule
rules.body: DSEG7 appears exactly once in the app: the Home kcal master readout. A second seven-segment element anywhere devalues the gauge.

rules.name: The Faceplate Rule
rules.body: Readings that belong to one instrument share one plate, divided internally by seams (divide-x/divide-y, edge-to-edge via negative margins) — never a stack of adjacent cards. Home's TODAY cluster (readout + scale + macro row + provenance footer) and Health's THIS WEEK cluster (average + sparkline + metric grid + counters row) are the canonical faceplates. One hero cluster per screen.

rules.name: The Band Rhythm
rules.body: The page stacks in functional bands — MEASURE → ASSESS → MOTIVATE/GUIDE — on a two-step cadence: 8px pairs modules within a band (wrapper space-y-2 or -mt-3 against a 20px stack), 20px separates bands (root space-y-5); 12px remains the interior content rhythm only. A constant gap between all modules is the card-soup tell this rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The Recessed Bay Rule
rules.body: Standby, empty, and not-yet-powered regions render as recessed wells (bg-plate-well, seam border, no plate) — an unpowered slot in the face, never a full module pretending to hold content.

rules.name: Panel Printing
rules.body: A sparse operative surface carries silkscreened panel material — process steps (01/02/03 rows), capability lines — printed as seam-divided module footers, the way hardware prints its diagrams; content, never decoration.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Separation is always a 1px seam or a tonal step, never a drop shadow, glow, or blur (backdrop-blur on the top status bar is the sole blur, and it blurs content, not edges).

rules.name: The Crisp Motion Rule
rules.body: All motion draws from four durations (100/160/320/420ms) and three curves (travel, arrive, exit) — never springy, bouncy, or decoratively looping. Every authored move degrades under prefers-reduced-motion to opacity-only or nothing, without losing state feedback.

rules.name: The Bolted Chassis Rule
rules.body: The chassis (top bar, control strip) never moves; the plate stack (<main>) travels as a PAIR — the outgoing plate is cloned into a fixed .plate-ghost clip layer across the body swap so old and new move together like a native OS stack. push-fwd/push-back between sibling tabs by key order (incoming full-width, outgoing 32% parallax + dim); cover: a tool rises over the visibly receding desk; uncover: the tool slides off downward over the brightening desk. Fade is reserved for non-spatial relationships — never the default.

rules.name: The Wipe Rule
rules.body: A wipe is the language of background work, never decoration: wipe-busy tracks a scanline across anything analysing off-screen; wipe-in reveals a freshly settled result once. Disclosures split open; new rows slot in. All motion rides transform/opacity/clip-path — plates never animate layout.

rules.name: The Honest Blank Rule
rules.body: An unknown value renders as '----' (or '—', an unlit LED, an empty seam-colored track) in ink-faint. The machine never draws a zero, a guessed bar, or a placeholder number for data it doesn't hold.

dos: Do open every module with a silkscreen micro-label (Fragment Mono 11px, 0.14em, uppercase, ink-faint) at top-left; modules self-identify.
Do set every measured value in Fragment Mono with tabular-nums, with units small and ink-dim beside the number, and provenance in an 11px uppercase mono line.
Do separate with 1px seams and tonal steps (well/plate/raised); keep the Band Rhythm (8px pairs, 20px bands, 12px interior).
Do put black type on any signal fill, and keep signal areas small — a chip, an LED, a marker line, a key.
Do render unknowns as '----' / 'NO DATA' / unlit cells, and quantize charts into cell stacks and tick scales.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion for every authored animation.
donts: Don't add drop shadows, glows, or gradients; the only shadow is the action key's machined ledge, and it stays on keys.
Don't use signal colors decoratively, as washes, or with shifted meanings; the only large signal field is the earned green success stamp.
Don't fire reward grammar (green field, LED sweep, stamp, ticking counters) without a genuine success trigger, and never use confetti or springy easing.
Don't set a number in Archivo or a sentence in Fragment Mono, and never use DSEG7 outside the single Home kcal readout.
Don't introduce a light mode, an appearance toggle, or pill radii (>6px corners); the world is one committed dark console.
Don't use icon fonts or filled glyph icons; icons are inline stroked SVGs in currentColor.
